segmentation.text: upon the right half of crosswalks.

elements.justification: 'Pedestrians' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate', claimed by its admitted id and never expanded into class atoms.

'shall move' places the duty on the pedestrian's movement: it is read at observations at which the pedestrian moves, i.e. where drv.motion.complete_halt ('The road user is at rest at the observation ... its speed (kin.speed) at or below a tolerance the caller sets for the source's speed resolution') does not hold with p.halt_speed_tolerance. A pedestrian at rest does not move, and the words place on it no duty of position.

'crosswalks' is st.crosswalk ('marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection'), carrying both limbs of DEF-NRS-484A-065 (the connection of the sidewalk lines at an intersection; a portion distinctly indicated for crossing by markings); the pedestrian's own crosswalk is anchored by rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'). 'the right half' is read about the crosswalk's reference point (st.region_geometry: 'the reference point and the boundary polygon of a structure region in the world frame'; its not-a-stand-in clause excludes occupancy, which rel.occupies reads) and the pedestrian's own direction of movement (kin.velocity 'velocity vector', kin.position 'position of the body's reference point', kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity'): the pedestrian is on the right half where the crosswalk's reference point does not lie to the right of its direction of movement by more than p.pedestrian_lateral_tolerance, i.e. v_x(r_y-p_y) - v_y(r_x-p_x) is at least minus that tolerance times its speed.

operationalizations.convention: pedestrian stride and shy distance: keeping to the right half is impracticable where the right half ahead of the pedestrian is taken up within about two strides, by another road user occupying the same crosswalk ahead on its right (rel.bearing: positive longitudinal and negative lateral component; rel.surface_gap at or below the reach) or by an obstruction on its right (prim.region_lateral_offset below zero; st.region_geometry distance at or below the reach)

applicability: The subject, a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian), occupies a crosswalk x (rel.occupies(subject, x), x of kind st.crosswalk) and moves: drv.motion.complete_halt(subject; p.halt_speed_tolerance) does not hold.
obligation: For every crosswalk x the subject occupies (re-bound with the same selection), either (a) it moves on the right half of x: with v its velocity, p its position and r the reference point of x, v_x*(r_y - p_y) - v_y*(r_x - p_x) is at least minus p.pedestrian_lateral_tolerance times its speed (kin.speed), so that x's reference point does not lie to its right by more than the tolerance; or (b) keeping to the right half is not practicable: some other road user u (not the subject) occupying x lies ahead of the subject on its right (rel.bearing(subject, u) with longitudinal component above zero and lateral component below zero) at a surface gap (rel.surface_gap) at or below p.pedestrian_near_reach, or some region o of kind st.obstruction lies on the subject's right (prim.region_lateral_offset(subject, o) below zero) at a ground distance (st.region_geometry) at or below p.pedestrian_near_reach.

narrowings.why: The halves of a crosswalk are read about its mapped reference point, taken as its centre, and the side is read relative to the pedestrian's own direction of movement (its velocity), which on a crossing runs along the crosswalk's length; a pedestrian within p.pedestrian_lateral_tolerance of the centre counts as on the right half.

The words name no factor of practicability; the catch-all is read only through the occupation of the right side ahead by another road user in the crosswalk or by an obstruction within p.pedestrian_near_reach; any other reason the right half may be impracticable is not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian (ru.aggregate pedestrian) walks across a marked crosswalk it occupies (rel.occupies st.crosswalk) at 1.3 m/s (kin.speed); the crosswalk's reference point (st.region_geometry) lies 1.5 m to the right of its velocity; no other road user and no st.obstruction is in the scene.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same pedestrian walks across the crosswalk with its reference point 1.5 m to the left of its velocity: it moves on the right half.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian walks along a st.sidewalk and occupies no st.crosswalk.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian moving in a crosswalk at 1.3 m/s whose velocity is not observed: which half it moves on cannot be read.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian moves on the left half of the crosswalk while three other pedestrians occupying the crosswalk lie ahead of it on its right (rel.bearing longitudinal positive, lateral negative) at a surface gap of 1.5 m: the right half is not practicable.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian stands at rest (kin.speed 0) on the left half of the crosswalk: it does not move.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of tracked-object kinematics in driving datasets and simulators

param_proposals.name: p.pedestrian_lateral_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the lateral margin within which a pedestrian's reference point counts as on a line that divides a region or a way: half a pedestrian's shoulder breadth plus the source's position error for a pedestrian
param_proposals.source: Highway Capacity Manual pedestrian body ellipse (about 0.6 m shoulder breadth) and pedestrian tracking position error

param_proposals.name: p.pedestrian_near_reach
param_proposals.convention: the ground distance from a pedestrian's body to a place, a region or a vehicle within which the pedestrian is near it: about two walking strides plus a curb step
param_proposals.source: pedestrian stride length (about 0.75 m) and curb step conventions of pedestrian facility design

segmentation.text: Except as otherwise provided in subsection 6 [NRS-484B-297-6],
shall walk on the left side of those highways facing the approaching traffic.

elements.justification: 'pedestrians' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'); ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate', never expanded into classes.

As the index maps 'to walk along and upon an adjacent roadway' (LVMC_11_30_090): 'highways' is st.highway ('the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders'; the definition's 'entire width between the boundary lines'), the pedestrian's own highway anchored by rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'); 'walking' is moving, drv.motion.complete_halt not holding; 'along' is moving not across the lanes of that highway beside it: for no lane (st.lane 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles') lying on the highway (st.on_way 'the public way ... a structure region lies on') within p.pedestrian_near_reach of the pedestrian's body (st.region_geometry 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it') does drv.motion.moving_across_carrier ('a moves across the designated direction of travel of carrier region r') hold. The lane is not read as a half of the roadway: it only gives the direction of travel along the way. The reach selects the lanes beside the pedestrian; belonging to the highway is st.on_way, not distance.

As the index maps 'Where sidewalks are provided' (LVMC_11_30_090): 'sidewalks' is st.sidewalk ('area for pedestrians between roadway and property line'; the definition's 'portion of a highway between the curb lines ... and the adjacent property lines intended for the use of pedestrians'), tied to the pedestrian's highway by st.on_way; the condition holds where no sidewalk lies on that highway. A crosswalk, which st.sidewalk is not a stand-in for, is not read.

'the left side of those highways' (the highway the pedestrian occupies, rel.occupies, st.highway), as the index maps 'must not be driven to the left side of the highway' (NRS_484B_213_2a): read against its st.centre_line ('the marking, or the geometric centre, dividing the two directions of a two-way roadway') lying on it (st.on_way), through prim.region_lateral_offset ('the signed lateral offset (m, left positive) of a structure region from a road user', perpendicular to its heading): the pedestrian walks on the left side when the centre line is not on its left, its offset being at most p.pedestrian_lateral_tolerance; 'left' is relative to the pedestrian's own direction of walking. 'facing the approaching traffic' is read through the designated direction of the lanes of that highway beside the pedestrian (st.lane on it by st.on_way, within p.pedestrian_near_reach of its body by st.region_geometry): drv.motion.moving_against_carrier ('Road user a moves against the designated direction of travel of carrier region r') holds for each, so the traffic those lanes carry approaches the pedestrian from the front. The word 'traffic' names the stream the lanes carry; the duty is the same whether or not a road user is approaching, so no road user is quantified.

applicability: The subject, a pedestrian, occupies a highway h (rel.occupies, st.highway) on which no sidewalk lies (no st.sidewalk s with st.on_way(s, h)); it walks: drv.motion.complete_halt(subject; p.halt_speed_tolerance) does not hold; and it walks along h: for no lane l lying on h (st.on_way(l, h)) whose ground distance from the subject's body (st.region_geometry) is at most p.pedestrian_near_reach does drv.motion.moving_across_carrier(subject, l; p.halt_speed_tolerance, p.crossing_motion_cos) hold. Not where NRS_484B_297_6_o1 or NRS_484B_297_6_o2 applies to the subject (exception compositions: subsection 6, a pedestrian moving around an obstruction to the sidewalk).
obligation: For every highway h the subject occupies on which no sidewalk lies (re-bound with the same selection): (left side) for every centre line c lying on h (st.centre_line, st.on_way(c, h)), prim.region_lateral_offset(subject, c) is at most p.pedestrian_lateral_tolerance: the centre line is not on the subject's left, so the subject walks on the left side of h relative to its direction of walking; and (facing the approaching traffic) for every lane l lying on h whose ground distance from the subject's body is at most p.pedestrian_near_reach, drv.motion.moving_against_carrier(subject, l; p.halt_speed_tolerance) holds.

narrowings.why: On a highway with no centre line (a one-way highway, where no line divides two directions) the left side is not read through a centre line and the duty is read through the facing element alone. The approaching traffic is read as the stream the lanes beside the pedestrian (within p.pedestrian_near_reach) carry in their designated direction; lanes farther from the pedestrian are not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian walks at 1.4 m/s along the shoulder of a two-lane two-way st.highway on which no st.sidewalk lies; the st.centre_line lies 4 m to its left (prim.region_lateral_offset +4 m); the near st.lane, 0.8 m from its body, has a designated direction (st.lane_direction) the same as the pedestrian's velocity. No other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian walks along the other shoulder: the centre line lies 4 m to its right (offset -4 m) and the near lane's designated direction is opposed to its velocity.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian walks along a highway on which a st.sidewalk lies (st.on_way).

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian walking along the shoulder of a highway with no sidewalk whose velocity is not observed: whether it walks along the way and faces the lanes' traffic cannot be read.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian stands at rest (kin.speed 0) on the right-hand shoulder of a highway with no sidewalk.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian crosses the highway: its velocity is perpendicular to the near lane's designated direction (drv.motion.moving_across_carrier holds).

segmentation.text: Whenever signals are placed over the individual lanes of a highway,
the signals indicate, and apply to
A downward-pointing green arrow means that
may drive in any lane over which the green signal is shown.

elements.justification: 'signals ... placed over the individual lanes' is dev.lane_control_signal ('an overhead per-lane signal'), the lane it is over read by dev.governs ('the travel regions whose traffic the device controls — a lane ...'; not a stand-in for a position, and no halt position is read); 'lanes of a highway' is st.lane ('a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles') lying on a st.highway ('the entire public way between its boundary lines') by st.on_way ('the public way ... a structure region lies on'). The lane is used as a lane, not as a half of the roadway.

'drivers of vehicles' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading): the subject is a member of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', its exclusions decided by the reading); 'driver' is not an aggregate.

'A downward-pointing green arrow' is the state green_down_arrow of dev.lane_control_signal ('state ∈ {green_down_arrow, red_x, yellow_x, yellow_arrow(dir), dark}') displayed by a head placed over a lane (dev.governs, st.lane).

As the index maps 'pedestrians facing the signal' (NRS_484B_283_1d1): facing is read from the head's location (dev.position 'location of the device head / sign face'; not a stand-in for a stop line or a crossing, none is read) and the subject's position and heading (kin.position, kin.heading 'direction the body points'): the head lies ahead of the subject, the dot product of the vector from the subject to the head with the subject's heading being positive. No atom carries the orientation of a signal face; a head ahead of the driver is the head it faces.

'drive in any lane' is the subject's footprint overlapping a lane (rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region', st.lane) while it moves (drv.motion.complete_halt does not hold: 'at rest at the observation ... speed at or below a tolerance'); 'over which the green signal is shown' is the lane-control signal (dev.lane_control_signal) placed over that lane (dev.governs) displaying green_down_arrow.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle); some lane l (st.lane) lying on a highway (st.on_way, st.highway) has a lane-control signal d placed over it (dev.lane_control_signal d, dev.governs(d, l)) that displays green_down_arrow and faces the subject: the dot product of (dev.position of d minus kin.position of the subject) with the subject's kin.heading is above zero; and the subject drives in a lane l2 (rel.occupies(subject, l2), st.lane) over which a lane-control signal d2 is placed (dev.governs(d2, l2)) that displays a state other than dark and faces the subject in the same way, while drv.motion.complete_halt(subject; p.halt_speed_tolerance) does not hold.
obligation: For every lane l2 and lane-control signal d2 so selected (re-bound with the whole selection: the subject occupies l2 while moving, d2 governs l2, is lit and faces the subject): d2 displays green_down_arrow — the lane the subject drives in is one over which the green signal is shown, the scope of the permission the words grant to a driver facing a green arrow.

narrowings.why: The words grant a permission and impose no duty of their own. The permission is read as its scope: a driver facing a green downward arrow, driving in a signalled lane under a lit head that faces it, is within the permission where the green arrow is shown over that lane; driving in a signalled lane under any other lit indication is outside it and is reported as a violation of this rule. Whether that conduct is also forbidden is decided by the rules of the other indications (NRS 484B.307(12)(b) and the following paragraphs).
'drivers' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle moving in the lane is taken to be driven, whoever or whatever is at its controls.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A vehicle (ru.aggregate vehicle) drives at 15 m/s in a st.lane over which a dev.lane_control_signal 80 m ahead (dev.position ahead along kin.heading, dev.governs that lane) displays yellow_x, while the signal over the adjacent lane, also ahead, displays green_down_arrow. No other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same vehicle drives in the lane whose overhead lane-control signal ahead displays green_down_arrow.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The vehicle drives on a road over whose lanes no lane-control signal is placed (no dev.governs from any dev.lane_control_signal).

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The vehicle drives in a lane of a road whose lane-control signals are not observed by the source: whether a signal is over the lane and what it shows cannot be read.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Every lane-control signal over the lanes ahead of the vehicle displays red_x: the driver faces no green arrow.

param_proposals.source: speed resolution of tracked-object kinematics in driving datasets and simulators

segmentation.text: Whenever signals are placed over the individual lanes of a highway,
the signals indicate, and apply to
must not enter or drive in any lane over which the red signal is shown.

elements.justification: 'signals ... placed over the individual lanes' is dev.lane_control_signal ('an overhead per-lane signal'), the lane it is over read by dev.governs ('the travel regions whose traffic the device controls — a lane ...'; not a stand-in for a position, and no halt position is read); 'lanes of a highway' is st.lane ('a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles') lying on a st.highway by st.on_way ('the public way ... a structure region lies on'). The lane is used as a lane, not as a half of the roadway.

'drivers of vehicles' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading): the subject is a member of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); 'driver' is not an aggregate.
'A red “X” symbol' is the state red_x of dev.lane_control_signal ('state ∈ {green_down_arrow, red_x, yellow_x, yellow_arrow(dir), dark}').

As the index maps 'pedestrians facing the signal' (NRS_484B_283_1d1): facing is read from the head's location (dev.position 'location of the device head / sign face'; not a stand-in for a stop line or crossing, none is read) and the subject's kin.position and kin.heading ('direction the body points'): the head lies ahead of the subject, the dot product of the vector from the subject to the head with its heading being positive. No atom carries the orientation of a signal face; a head ahead of the driver is the head it faces.

'enter ... any lane' is the rise of the subject's footprint overlap with the lane (rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'); 'drive in' is the overlap while the subject moves (drv.motion.complete_halt — 'at rest at the observation' — not holding with p.halt_speed_tolerance); 'over which the red signal is shown' is the lane governed (dev.governs) by the lane-control signal displaying red_x.

applicability: The subject is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle), and some lane l (st.lane) lying on a highway (st.on_way, st.highway) has a lane-control signal d placed over it (dev.lane_control_signal d, dev.governs(d, l)) that displays red_x and faces the subject: the dot product of (dev.position of d minus kin.position of the subject) with the subject's kin.heading is above zero.
obligation: For every lane l and lane-control signal d so selected (re-bound with the whole selection: d governs l, displays red_x and faces the subject): the subject does not enter l — rel.occupies(subject, l) does not rise at the observation — and does not drive in l — it does not occupy l while drv.motion.complete_halt(subject; p.halt_speed_tolerance) fails.

narrowings.why: A vehicle that occupies a red-X lane while at rest (already in the lane when the indication appeared, halted) neither enters nor drives in it at that observation.
'drivers' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: a vehicle moving on the road is taken to be driven, whoever or whatever is at its controls.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A vehicle (ru.aggregate vehicle) moving at 15 m/s changes into a st.lane over which a dev.lane_control_signal 80 m ahead (dev.position ahead along kin.heading) displays red_x: rel.occupies of that lane rises. No other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The vehicle keeps to its own lane, whose signal displays green_down_arrow, while the signal over the adjacent lane displays red_x; it never occupies the red-X lane.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: No lane-control signal in the scene displays red_x.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The vehicle drives on a road whose lane-control signals are not observed by the source.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The vehicle already occupies a lane when its overhead signal ahead turns to red_x and keeps driving in it at 12 m/s.

segmentation.text: When the signal is circular green alone:
may proceed straight through or turn right or left
unless another device at the place prohibits either or both such turns.
Such vehicular traffic, including vehicles turning right or left,
lawfully within the intersection or an adjacent crosswalk at the time the signal is exhibited.

elements.justification: 'the signal is circular green alone' is dev.traffic_signal ('a signal head; state ∈ {circular_green, ... green_arrow(dir) ...}; several states may be displayed at once') displaying circular_green and no other state: 'alone' excludes a green arrow or any other state shown with it.

'Vehicular traffic' is a member of the admitted aggregates DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel') and DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported'), both claimed as ru.aggregate and never expanded. 'facing the signal' is read through the approach: the subject occupies (rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') a carrier (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'; st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet'), and the signal governs that carrier (dev.governs 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'; not a stand-in for a position, none is read). The intersection is fixed by the carrier's entry topology, never by motion or distance.

'may proceed straight through or turn' names the traffic proceeding on its approach into and through the intersection, as the index maps 'approaching the intersection' (LVMC_11_12_070_B): the subject occupies the approach carrier entering the intersection (st.lane_enters), or occupies the intersection (rel.occupies, st.intersection) having been on that carrier continuously since; the movement it makes (straight or a turn) does not change the duty.

'Such vehicular traffic, including vehicles turning right or left' refers back to the subject (traffic aggregate and vehicle aggregate, 'membership of a legal aggregate'); the inclusion of turning vehicles adds no restriction: the duty binds the subject whichever movement it makes.

As the index maps 'shall yield the right-of-way' (NRS_484B_263_o1): to yield is to grant precedence — the subject does not move (kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while the danger of a crash with a protected party exists, and does not move into contact with it (rel.contact 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)'; not a stand-in for a near miss, which the operationalization of s7 reads).

'other vehicles' are road users other than the subject that are members of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('membership of a legal aggregate'; 'every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported'): the parties to whom the right-of-way is owed.

'pedestrians' are members of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'): the parties to whom the right-of-way is owed.

'within the intersection' is the party's footprint overlapping (rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') the intersection the subject approaches or occupies (st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet'; not a stand-in for a crosswalk, which is read separately); 'an adjacent crosswalk' is a st.crosswalk ('marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection') tied to that intersection by relation atoms: it marks the entrance (st.entrance_of 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks') of some carrier (st.travel_region) entering that intersection (st.lane_enters); distance is not read for belonging. 'at the time the signal is exhibited' reads the party's presence at the same observation as dev.traffic_signal displaying circular_green alone ('several states may be displayed at once'). 'lawfully' is read as the operationalization of s7 discloses.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: 'approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other')
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash with a party exists where, under constant velocities, the centres of the subject and the party approach within the conflict horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below the conflict clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance), which reads the direction, the speed and the proximity of both together

residues.why: The words limit the permission to turn, not the duty to yield: traffic facing the circular green must yield whether or not another device prohibits a turn, and whether it makes the turn or not; the duty is the same either way.

applicability: There are an intersection i (st.intersection), a carrier c (st.travel_region) entering i (st.lane_enters(c, i)) and a traffic signal d (dev.traffic_signal) governing c (dev.governs(d, c)) such that d displays circular_green and no other state at the observation, and the subject, a member of traffic and a vehicle, either occupies c (rel.occupies(subject, c)) or occupies i and has occupied i continuously since an observation at which it occupied c (rel.occupies(subject, i) since rel.occupies(subject, c)).
obligation: Re-binding i, c and d with the whole selection of the applicability: for every road user u other than the subject that is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) or a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) and that occupies i, or occupies a crosswalk x (st.crosswalk) marking the entrance (st.entrance_of(x, c2)) of some carrier c2 entering i (st.lane_enters(c2, i)): it is not the case that the subject moves (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while either prim.closest_approach_within(subject, u; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, u; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance, or rel.contact(subject, u) holds.

narrowings.why: The right-of-way is owed to the parties s8 to s10 name; their 'lawfully' is not read: the words name no rule whose verdict decides a party's lawfulness, so every vehicle or pedestrian within is owed it; the rule never excuses a failure to yield to a lawful party and reaches further only where a party's presence is unlawful. 'an adjacent crosswalk' is any crosswalk that marks the entrance of a carrier into the same intersection; 'at the time the signal is exhibited' is every observation at which the circular green is displayed alone. Direction, speed and proximity are read together through the constant-velocity closest approach of the centres; a change of speed or direction ahead is not anticipated.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject vehicle occupies an approach lane entering an intersection whose dev.traffic_signal (dev.governs the lane) displays circular_green alone; it turns left into the intersection at 6 m/s while a pedestrian (ru.aggregate pedestrian) walks in the crosswalk that marks the entrance of the cross street's approach (st.entrance_of); prim.closest_approach_within holds with a closest centre distance of 1.0 m in 1.5 s, and the subject keeps moving.

scenarios.name: permit

segmentation.text: When the signal is circular green alone:
within any marked or unmarked crosswalk,
unless directed otherwise by another device as provided in NRS 484B.283 [NRS-484B-283-1d1, NRS-484B-283-1d2, NRS-484B-283-1d3, NRS-484B-283-1d4].

elements.justification: 'the signal is circular green alone' is dev.traffic_signal ('a signal head; state ∈ {circular_green, ...}; several states may be displayed at once') displaying circular_green and no other state.

'Pedestrians' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'), 'membership of a legal aggregate'.

As the index maps 'pedestrians facing the signal' (NRS_484B_283_1d1): facing is read from the head's location (dev.position 'location of the device head / sign face'; not a stand-in for a stop line or crossing, none is read) and the pedestrian's kin.position and kin.heading ('direction the body points'): the head lies within p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_reach of the pedestrian and within the angle whose cosine is p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_cos of its heading (compared on squares: the dot product of the vector to the head with the heading is positive and its square at least that cosine squared times the vector's squared length). No atom carries the orientation of a signal face; the head ahead of the pedestrian within that angle is the head it faces.

As the index maps 'crossing a roadway' (LVMC_11_30_060_A): proceeding across the highway is the pedestrian occupying (rel.occupies) a lane (st.lane 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles') of a roadway (st.roadway 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic') while drv.motion.moving_across_carrier ('a moves across the designated direction of travel of carrier region r') holds for that lane: the crossing of the highway is observed where it traverses the highway's lanes of travel. The lane is not read as a half of the roadway; st.roadway is not a stand-in for a sidewalk, which the crossing does not use.

'within any marked or unmarked crosswalk' is the pedestrian's footprint overlapping a st.crosswalk ('marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection; marked attribute'), which carries both limbs of DEF-NRS-484A-065; rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'.

applicability: Some traffic signal d (dev.traffic_signal) displays circular_green and no other state; the subject, a pedestrian, faces d: d's head (dev.position) lies within p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_reach of the subject's kin.position and within the angle whose cosine is p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_cos of its kin.heading; and the subject proceeds across the highway: it occupies a lane l of a roadway (rel.occupies, st.lane, st.roadway) and drv.motion.moving_across_carrier(subject, l; p.halt_speed_tolerance, p.crossing_motion_cos) holds. Not where any of NRS_484B_283_1d1, NRS_484B_283_1d2, NRS_484B_283_1d3_o1, NRS_484B_283_1d3_o2, NRS_484B_283_1d4_o1 or NRS_484B_283_1d4_o2 applies to the subject (exception compositions: another device directs the pedestrian as NRS 484B.283 provides).
obligation: The subject occupies a crosswalk (rel.occupies(subject, x) for some x of kind st.crosswalk, marked or unmarked): the crossing it makes under the circular green is within the scope of the permission the words grant.

narrowings.why: The words grant a permission and impose no duty of their own. The permission is read as its scope: a crossing of the highway by a pedestrian facing a circular green alone is within it where the pedestrian is within a marked or unmarked crosswalk; a crossing outside every crosswalk is outside the permission and is reported as a violation of this rule. Whether that crossing is also forbidden is decided by the rules on crossing elsewhere (NRS 484B.287).

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A pedestrian (ru.aggregate pedestrian) crosses a st.lane of a st.roadway at 1.3 m/s perpendicular to its designated direction (drv.motion.moving_across_carrier holds), 30 m from any st.crosswalk, facing a dev.traffic_signal head 25 m ahead (dev.position within the facing angle) that displays circular_green alone; no pedestrian signal governs; no other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same pedestrian makes the same crossing within a marked crosswalk (rel.occupies st.crosswalk).

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The signal the pedestrian faces displays circular_red.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The pedestrian crosses outside a crosswalk while a signal displays circular_green alone, but the positions of the signal heads are not observed: whether it faces the signal cannot be read.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A dev.pedestrian_signal governing the crossing displays dont_walk_steady, so NRS_484B_283_1d4_o1 applies to the pedestrian: another device directs it, and this rule does not apply.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of tracked-object kinematics in driving datasets and simulators

param_proposals.name: p.crossing_motion_cos
param_proposals.convention: largest absolute cosine between a pedestrian's velocity and a carrier's designated direction at which the pedestrian counts as moving across the carrier rather than along it: motion more than about 20 degrees away from the direction of travel
param_proposals.source: pedestrian trajectory heading variability reported in crossing-behaviour studies

param_proposals.name: p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_cos
param_proposals.convention: cosine of the largest angle (about thirty degrees) between a pedestrian's heading and the line from its position to a vehicular signal head at which the pedestrian counts as facing that head: the lateral offset of a far-side head from the crossing's line plus a pedestrian's heading wander
param_proposals.source: MUTCD signal head placement (Part 4D) and pedestrian heading variability

param_proposals.name: p.ped_traffic_signal_facing_reach
param_proposals.convention: the largest distance from a pedestrian to a vehicular signal head at which the head counts as one the pedestrian faces across the intersection: a wide urban intersection (about 40 m) plus the set-back of a far-side head beyond the far crosswalk
param_proposals.source: MUTCD far-side signal head placement (Part 4D) and urban intersection widths

segmentation.text: Where the signal is circular green with a green turn arrow:
to make the movement indicated by the green turn arrow or such other movement as is permitted by the circular green signal,
at the time the signal is exhibited.

Drivers turning in the direction of the arrow when displayed with the circular green are thereby advised that so long as a turn arrow is illuminated, oncoming or opposing traffic simultaneously faces a steady red signal.

elements.justification: 'circular green with a green turn arrow' is dev.traffic_signal ('a signal head; state ∈ {circular_green, ... green_arrow(dir) ...} with dir ∈ {left, right, straight, u_turn}; several states may be displayed at once') displaying circular_green together with green_arrow(dir) for a turn direction (left, right or u_turn; a straight arrow is no turn arrow).

'Vehicular traffic' is a member of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel') that is a vehicle: 'vehicular' uses the defined word of DEF-NRS-484A-320, whose admitted id DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway') is claimed (see PLAN.md). 'facing the signal' is read through the approach: the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a carrier (st.travel_region) whose entrance end is the intersection (st.lane_enters 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'; st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet') and the signal governs that carrier (dev.governs 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'; not a stand-in for a position).

'may proceed' names the traffic proceeding on its approach into and through the intersection, as the index maps 'approaching the intersection' (LVMC_11_12_070_B): the subject occupies the approach carrier entering the intersection (st.lane_enters), or occupies the intersection (rel.occupies, st.intersection) having been on that carrier continuously since.
'the traffic' refers back to the subject, a member of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('membership of a legal aggregate').

As the index maps 'shall yield the right-of-way' (NRS_484B_263_o1): the subject does not move (kin.speed 'magnitude of velocity' above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while the danger of a crash with a protected party exists, and does not move into contact with it (rel.contact 'touch or overlap (a collision)'; not a stand-in for a near miss, which s7's operationalization reads).

'pedestrians' are members of DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian ('a person afoot, a person in a manual or motorized wheelchair, or a person on an electric personal assistive mobility device'): parties to whom the right-of-way is owed.

'within an adjacent crosswalk' is the pedestrian's footprint overlapping (rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') a st.crosswalk ('marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection') tied to the intersection by relation atoms: it marks the entrance (st.entrance_of 'the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks') of some carrier (st.travel_region) entering that intersection (st.lane_enters); distance is not read for belonging. 'lawfully' is read as the narrowing on s7 discloses.

'other traffic' are road users other than the subject that are members of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel'): parties to whom the right-of-way is owed.

'using the intersection' is the party's footprint overlapping the intersection the subject approaches or occupies (rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'; st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet', not a stand-in for a crosswalk). 'lawfully' is read as the narrowing on s7 discloses.

'at the time the signal is exhibited' reads the parties' presence at the same observation as dev.traffic_signal displaying circular_green with a green turn arrow ('several states may be displayed at once').

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: 'approaching under such circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash unless one grants precedence to the other')
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash with a party exists where, under constant velocities, the centres of the subject and the party approach within the conflict horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below the conflict clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance), which reads the direction, the speed and the proximity of both together

residues.why: The words describe which movements the traffic may make (the arrow's movement or one the circular green permits); the duty to yield binds the traffic facing the signal whichever movement it makes, so the duty is the same whether or not the movement is one of those.

An advisory statement of the signal phasing for the driver's information (opposing traffic faces a steady red while the arrow is lit); it requires, permits or forbids nothing, and the duty to yield is the same whether or not it holds.

applicability: There are an intersection i (st.intersection), a carrier c (st.travel_region) entering i (st.lane_enters(c, i)) and a traffic signal d (dev.traffic_signal) governing c (dev.governs(d, c)) such that d displays circular_green together with green_arrow(dir) for some dir among left, right and u_turn at the observation, and the subject, a member of traffic and a vehicle, either occupies c (rel.occupies(subject, c)) or occupies i and has occupied i continuously since an observation at which it occupied c (rel.occupies(subject, i) since rel.occupies(subject, c)).
obligation: Re-binding i, c and d with the whole selection of the applicability: for every road user u other than the subject that either is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) occupying a crosswalk x (st.crosswalk) marking the entrance (st.entrance_of(x, c2)) of some carrier c2 entering i (st.lane_enters(c2, i)), or is a member of traffic (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) occupying i: it is not the case that the subject moves (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while either prim.closest_approach_within(subject, u; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, u; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance, or rel.contact(subject, u) holds.

narrowings.why: The right-of-way is owed to the parties s9 to s13 name; their 'lawfully' (twice) is not read: the words name no rule whose verdict decides a party's lawfulness, so every pedestrian within an adjacent crosswalk and every member of traffic within the intersection is owed it; the rule reaches further than the words only where that presence is unlawful. 'an adjacent crosswalk' is any crosswalk marking the entrance of a carrier into the same intersection; 'at the time the signal is exhibited' is every observation at which the circular green with a green turn arrow is displayed. Direction, speed and proximity are read together through the constant-velocity closest approach of the centres.

segmentation.text: Where the signal is a green turn arrow alone:
may proceed only in the direction indicated by the arrow signal so long as the arrow is illuminated,
but the traffic must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians lawfully within the adjacent crosswalk and to other traffic lawfully using the intersection.

elements.justification: 'a green turn arrow alone' is dev.traffic_signal ('a signal head; state ∈ {... green_arrow(dir) ...} with dir ∈ {left, right, straight, u_turn}; several states may be displayed at once') displaying green_arrow(dir) for a turn direction (left, right or u_turn) and no other state: 'alone' excludes a circular green or any other state shown with it.

'Vehicular traffic' is a member of DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway for purposes of travel') that is a vehicle: 'vehicular' uses the defined word of DEF-NRS-484A-320, whose admitted id DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported') is claimed (see PLAN.md). 'facing the signal' is read through the approach: the subject's passage through the intersection (st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet') began from a carrier (st.travel_region) it occupied (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is that intersection (st.lane_enters 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end') and which the signal governs (dev.governs 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls'; not a stand-in for a position).

'proceed only in the direction indicated by the arrow' is the passage through the intersection matching the arrow's direction, read at its recognition, the subject's exit from the intersection (rel.occupies of st.intersection ceasing): for green_arrow(left), drv.motion.left_turn_through_region ('Road user a has made a turn to the left through region r, recognized as it leaves r'); for green_arrow(right), drv.motion.right_turn_through_region ('has made a turn to the right through region r'); for green_arrow(u_turn), drv.motion.u_turn_through_region ('has turned so as to proceed in the opposite direction through region r'), each over the intersection the subject passes, with step p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph, turn_min p.turn_heading_min and u_turn_min p.u_turn_heading_min. 'so long as the arrow is illuminated' is dev.traffic_signal displaying that arrow alone at some observation of the passage (the occasion of s1).

applicability: At an observation at which the subject, a member of traffic and a vehicle, exits an intersection i (st.intersection): rel.occupies(subject, i) does not hold, having held at the previous observation; its passage through i began from a carrier c (st.travel_region) entering i (st.lane_enters(c, i)) that it occupied at its entry into i (the observation at which rel.occupies(subject, i) rose); a traffic signal d (dev.traffic_signal) governs c (dev.governs(d, c)); and at some observation from that entry to the exit, d displayed green_arrow(dir) and no other state, for some dir among left, right and u_turn.
obligation: Re-binding i, c, d and dir with the whole selection of the applicability: the passage through i matches the arrow's direction at this exit: for dir left, drv.motion.left_turn_through_region(subject, i; p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph, p.turn_heading_min, p.u_turn_heading_min) holds; for dir right, drv.motion.right_turn_through_region(subject, i; p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph, p.turn_heading_min, p.u_turn_heading_min) holds; for dir u_turn, drv.motion.u_turn_through_region(subject, i; p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph, p.u_turn_heading_min) holds. Where arrows of several directions were displayed alone during the passage, matching any one of them complies.

narrowings.why: 'so long as the arrow is illuminated' is read as the arrow displayed alone at some observation of the subject's passage through the intersection, from its entry to its exit; a passage begun and ended while no such arrow is displayed is not judged. The direction is read on the whole passage, recognized at the exit.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject vehicle enters an intersection from an approach lane whose dev.traffic_signal displays green_arrow(left) alone and drives straight through: at its exit drv.motion.left_turn_through_region does not hold (heading change about 0 degrees). No other road user is in the scene.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same subject turns left through the intersection on the green left arrow alone: at its exit the heading change since its entry is about 90 degrees to the left.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The signal governing the subject's approach displays circular_green alone throughout its passage; the subject drives straight through.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject passes through the intersection on a green left arrow alone, but its yaw rate is not observed: the turn concepts cannot be decided at its exit.

scenarios.name: occasion_s1

scenarios.name: occasion_s1_outside
scenarios.narrative: The signal displays green_arrow(left) alone only before the subject enters the intersection and circular_red from its entry to its exit; the subject drives straight through: the arrow held only before the passage began.

onset.words: the subject's entry into the intersection: the observation at which its footprint came to overlap the intersection, having not overlapped it at the previous observation
onset.justification: The turn-through-region concepts state 'The act begins at the observation at which a's footprint came to overlap r (rel.occupies), having not overlapped it at the previous observation: its entry into r'; the region is the intersection (st.intersection) the subject passes.

occasion.recognition: the observation at which the subject's footprint does not overlap the intersection, having overlapped it at the previous observation: its exit, at which the turn concepts are recognized

under_way.words: an observation from the subject's entry into the intersection up to its exit, at which its heading change since the entry is being integrated from its yaw rate
under_way.justification: An observation inside the act is one since the subject's entry into the intersection (rel.occupies rose) and before its exit, over which the concepts integrate the subject's motion, its heading change from kin.yaw_rate ('rate of change of heading'); before the entry no heading change of the passage is accumulated.

param_proposals.name: p.turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change over the turn window at which a change of course counts as a turn rather than a lane change or a drift
param_proposals.source: intersection turn geometry: a lane change alters heading by a few degrees, a turn at a junction by about 90 degrees

param_proposals.name: p.u_turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change magnitude over the turn window at which a turn counts as a reversal of direction
param_proposals.source: intersection turn geometry: a left turn alters heading by about 90 degrees, a reversal by about 180 degrees

obligation: Re-binding i, c and d with the whole selection of the applicability: for every road user u other than the subject that either is a pedestrian (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-165::pedestrian) occupying a crosswalk x (st.crosswalk) marking the entrance (st.entrance_of(x, c2)) of some carrier c2 entering i (st.lane_enters(c2, i)), or is a member of traffic (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) occupying i: it is not the case that the subject moves (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while either prim.closest_approach_within(subject, u; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, u; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance, or rel.contact(subject, u) holds.

narrowings.why: The right-of-way is owed to the parties s7 to s10 name; their 'lawfully' (twice) is not read: the words name no rule whose verdict decides the party's lawfulness, so every pedestrian within an adjacent crosswalk and every member of traffic within the intersection is protected; the rule reaches further than the words only where that presence is unlawful. 'the adjacent crosswalk' — the words leave open which crosswalk the turning traffic crosses, its exit leg not being known before the turn ends — is read as every crosswalk marking the entrance of a carrier into the same intersection; the danger-of-crash bound selects the one the subject's path meets. Direction, speed and proximity are read together through the constant-velocity closest approach of the centres.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject vehicle occupies an approach lane whose dev.traffic_signal displays green_arrow(left) alone; it turns left at 6 m/s while a pedestrian walks in the crosswalk marking the entrance of the cross street's approach (st.entrance_of); prim.closest_approach_within holds with a closest centre distance of 1.0 m in 1.5 s, and the subject keeps moving.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject halts (kin.speed 0) short of the crosswalk until the pedestrian has crossed, then completes its turn with no closest approach below the clearance within the horizon.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The signal governing the subject's approach displays circular_red.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject turns at a signalized intersection whose signal states are not observed by the source.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: On the green left arrow alone the subject turns left; no other road user is in the scene.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of tracked-object kinematics in driving datasets and simulators

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic conflict technique (Hydén; time-to-collision thresholds of 1.5 to 3 s)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: AASHTO passenger-car design vehicle dimensions
